title: RAW UNREVIEWED: paragraph-conditioned p/y spelling under one shared lexical key
summary: Test a strict same-lexeme writing hypothesis for fixed pX/yX wholes: paragraph context may change the spelling channel, while a shared lexical or phonological decoding key must preserve the whole lexical content. This is a new conditional equality contract, not p=begin/y=continue or a discovered alphabet.

design.hypothesis: In a declared subset of the five GDT1074 bases, pX and yX are context-conditioned written realizations of the same lexical value. The subset must be frozen before semantic fitting. One channel rule and one key are shared across all complete passages; no pair-specific semantic synonym, local operand donation or changed predicate is permitted. Whole-form residuals must be paid rather than deleting p/y mechanically.
design.owned_observation: 1074 has robust paragraph-opening direction for aiin,chedy,cheol,cheor,chor;1075 retains matched section/hand direction.1099 provides one actual header/reprise opportunity f9v.5 pchor to .11 ychor in complete .5-.12, plus internal pchedy at f81r.8/.12 and reversed yaiin/paiin f86v6.39/.45. These are not established lexical equalities.
design.historical_prior: The already inspected 609 contextual abbreviation/position-sensitive writing families motivate separating a spelling convention from lexical meaning. They do not attest this exact p/y alternation or choose a source language.
design.changed_contract: Compared with 788 case/response or 757 take/further, both wholes must have identical lexical content; only a predeclared nonsemantic writing-context rule differs. Compared with 338, test complete decoded lexical/argument consequences under a shared key, not statistical exchangeability of opaque renderer tuples.
design.discriminating_data_path: Root may first inspect the already owned complete1099 f9v .5-.12 and the two reversed/internal countercontexts without new access. A separately frozen lexical analysis must give both forms the same value and full argument role across at least two nonseed complete consumers. An explicitly aligned historical enlarged-initial/plain-initial spelling pair, if later lawfully obtained, can constrain the channel; an unrelated ornament alone cannot.
design.falsifier: Reject this declared equality channel if complete source-backed grammatical analyses require different lexical values or if preserving equality requires a new context exception, free residual or pair-specific key. UNKNOWN lexical analyses remain unknown. A universal paragraph-start switch already conflicts with internal p and reversed ordering and is not proposed.
gaps: No identified alphabet, source language, phonology or same-lexeme binding
